title: Extension after parallel coordinate fixing
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho,\tau:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{fix\ one},\mathrm{fix\ negative\ one}\}$, and let $L$ be a list of distinct coordinates in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For $x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$, suppose fixing the coordinates in $L$ in $\rho$ according to the signs encoded by $x$ gives a restriction extended by $\tau$. Then fixing those coordinates in both $\rho$ and $\tau$ according to the signs encoded by $y$ gives restrictions such that the one obtained from $\tau$ extends the one obtained from $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: A list $L$ with no repeated coordinates
The restriction obtained by fixing $\rho$ along $L$ according to $x$ is extended by $\tau$
